title: Arrow and reference line
text: The basic welding-symbol arrangement includes an arrow line with an arrowhead and a reference line. The arrowhead touches the component surfaces at the intended weld location.

title: Supplementary information
text: Extra details about a weld can be written in the tail of its welding symbol.

title: Process number example
text: Welding-process identifiers can appear in the symbol tail. In the example discussed by the article, process number 135 denotes MAG welding.

title: Intermittent fillet dimensions
text: Numbers to the right of a welding symbol describe longitudinal dimensions. For intermittent fillet welds these include weld count, segment length, and spacing.

title: Staggered fillet arrangement
text: For fillet welds on both faces of a joint, a Z crossing the reference line indicates a staggered arrangement.

title: Side convention in the historical review
text: The article describes BS 499 and AWS notation with symbols below the reference line for the arrow side and above it for the other side. This is a 2020 explanatory review, not the current standard text.
